subject: Clarify EOD inclusivity / timezone for SOC 2 Type II coverage window
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acme.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Martin <paul@auditsplus.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: SOC 2 report — is June 30 inclusive of all events for the period?

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're preparing our compliance tracker: your SOC 2 Type II report lists the audit period as Jan 1, 2024 through Jun 30, 2024. Can you confirm whether the coverage is inclusive of events that occurred on Jun 30 in any timezone (e.g., would an event that happened 2024-06-30 23:59 PST be considered within scope), or do you treat the end date as a point-in-time snapshot at a specific timestamp? Also, our security team is asking whether bridge letters are provided for gaps or cutoff clarifications, and whether those letters reference a timezone/UTC timestamp.

We'd like to finalize our evidence request list today; Paul can pull the report once we understand the cutoff semantics.

Thanks,
Karen

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@acme.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, Paul Martin <paul@auditsplus.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report — is June 30 inclusive of all events for the period?

Hi Karen,

Thanks for flagging this — great question. Short answer: the audit period in the PDF is intended to be inclusive of the full calendar day in UTC for the end date, and we provide a bridge letter when customers request explicit timestamp language. A few specifics so your team can map to their event logs:

- Coverage stated in the report (e.g., "Jan 1, 2024 through Jun 30, 2024") is inclusive of events that occur up to 23:59:59 UTC on Jun 30, 2024.
- Auditor testing uses a mix of period population testing and point-in-time checks. For point-in-time controls, the auditor may reference the last second of the day in UTC (we will confirm the exact timestamp they recorded).
- If your systems record in PST/PDT, convert to UTC for an exact mapping (Jun 30 23:59 PDT = Jul 1 06:59 UTC during daylight savings).

We can provide a short bridge letter that spells out the explicit UTC cutoff if that helps with your tracker. I attached the most recent draft we share with customers and the stub report for reference.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will ask Neha to confirm the auditor's recorded timestamp for point-in-time tests and confirm whether any exceptions were scoped to local time versus UTC.
2) If you want formal wording, we can send the bridge letter with exact UTC cutoff language and sign-off from our compliance lead.

Would you like the bridge letter to say "inclusive through 2024-06-30T23:59:59Z" or to reference "end of day, June 30, 2024 (UTC)"? Either is fine on our side; we just want to match how your ingestion is set up.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Trust & Security, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report — is June 30 inclusive of all events for the period?

Hi Karen and team,

Following up with the auditor notes: I checked the workpapers and confirmed the following for our 2024 Type II engagement with AuditsPlus:

- The coverage end is inclusive through 2024-06-30 23:59:59 UTC.
- For controls that were tested as a point-in-time (e.g., access lists, snapshot-based config reviews), the auditor used the UTC timestamp above as the reference.
- For population-based testing (e.g., log populations, change windows), the sample frames included all events recorded during the inclusive period up to that timestamp.
- There were two minor exceptions that the auditor documented; neither affected end-of-day inclusivity, but we can share the exception summaries if helpful.

I attached a draft bridge letter that includes the explicit UTC wording and a short paragraph explaining how local timezone recordings should be converted. If Acme prefers to reference local time instead, we're happy to include both formats.

Let me know if you want the auditor to add the exact point-in-time timestamp to their signed bridge letter or if the unsigned draft is sufficient for your tracker.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
